title: Larkspur Neighborhood Access Grant Closing-Cost Share by Census Tract
content:
The share of the unpaid closing costs a Larkspur Neighborhood Access Grant pays follows the census tract income level of the property, as recorded on the borrower's Mortgage Loan File.

| Census tract income level | Closing-cost share |
|---|---|
| moderate | 90 percent of the unpaid closing costs |
| middle or upper (the grant is then qualified on income alone) | 80 percent |
| low | the whole of them |

**Clause.** A moderate-income tract takes 90 percent of the unpaid closing costs; a middle-income or upper-income tract, where the grant is qualified on income alone, takes 80 percent; a low-income tract takes the whole of them.

**Where the share acts.** The unpaid closing costs, once floored at zero, are multiplied by the grant's closing-cost share and rounded to the cent; the closing-cost entry is the lesser of the grant's available balance and that share of the unpaid closing costs.

### Worked example (hypothetical)

Unpaid closing costs of 4425.00 and an available balance of 5000.00:

| Tract level | Share of the unpaid closing costs | Entry |
|---|---|---|
| moderate | 3982.50 | 3982.50 |
| middle | 3540.00 | 3540.00 |
| low | 4425.00 | 4425.00 |

With an available balance of 3600.00 instead, the low-tract entry is 3600.00 and the moderate-tract entry 3600.00, the balance being the lesser figure; the middle-tract entry stays 3540.00.
